target_customer: Startups and SaaS companies that sign commercial contracts with customers and vendors
problem: Negotiating commercial contracts is slow and custom. Common Paper publishes standard open-source agreements with structured data and software to send and manage them.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for contract management and AI review, with free open standard contracts

founders.name: Jake Stein
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked in venture capital before RJMetrics.

technical_complexity.rationale: Contract templates plus a workflow and e-sign style app are standard SaaS engineering; the hard part is legal standardisation, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Open licence means templates are copyable, but adoption of a shared standard by 40,000+ companies (company claim) can create a network effect.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established CLM vendors existed but targeted larger firms; no evidence found of them copying the open standard model.

market_need_then: Sales cycles slow down in contract negotiation and startups lack legal resources; early users at the seed announcement included Figma, Crossbeam and Clickhouse.

identity.mascot_or_character: Gerri, an AI contract review agent (product persona)
identity.visual_style: Minimal layout with short bold headlines

branding.brand_signature: Positioned as the SAFE for commercial contracts
branding.community_and_virality: A Dribbble listing shows a Focus Lab branding project for Common Paper dated March 2022 (single designer side source); Figma counsel testimonial on the site.

brand_strength.rationale: The SAFE analogy gave a clear positioning and the standards are widely used by startups; the name itself is generic and independent press on the brand was limited.

outcome_analysis: Common Paper raised a $4.5M seed in March 2022 before joining YC in Winter 2023, founded by a serial founder with two prior exits. It has grown from free standard contracts to contract management and AI review, with named startup customers. No later priced round was found, so its funding coverage is partial.
notes: The seed round predates the YC batch by about 10 months. CB Insights lists a $0.5M convertible note in January 2023 with Y Combinator; this matches the standard YC deal and is not recorded as a round. No Series A found. Name origin not found. Jake Stein's prior employers are not listed on the YC page beyond his companies. Outcome search found no shutdown, acquisition or layoffs.
